evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/nfc/NFCAccessController.ts:275 — validateAccess() gates a physical-access NFC credential with `if (new Date(credential.validUntil) < now) { return { granted:false, denialReason:'credential_expired' } }`. `credential.validUntil` is typed `string` (nfc/types.ts:26) and is deserialized from a stored JSON blob. When that string is empty/missing/malformed, `new Date(validUntil)` is an Invalid Date, and `InvalidDate < now` evaluates to `false` (every relational comparison with NaN is false). The expiry branch is therefore SKIPPED, and — provided status==='active' and the access point matches — validateAccess returns granted:true. This is a FAIL-OPEN on a building-access decision: a credential with a corrupted/absent expiry is treated as not-expired rather than denied.

Asymmetry confirms intent: the sibling methods in nfc/NFCCredentialManager.ts use the opposite, fail-CLOSED idiom — getActiveCredentials (:143) keeps a credential only when `new Date(c.validUntil).getTime() > nowMs` (NaN > nowMs === false -> excluded), and isCredentialExpiringSoon (:319) computes `new Date(credential.validUntil).getTime()` likewise. Only the actual access-GRANT path (validateAccess) is written as `date < now`, which inverts the safe default exactly where it matters most.

Reachability: validateAccess is the tap-to-enter authorization check; credential.validUntil originates from persisted/offline-cached credential data (SecureStore/AsyncStorage JSON), which the same segment's other findings already show can be corrupted or legacy-shaped (see done rows nfc-securestore-2kb-blob, nfc-accesslog-parse-unguarded). Net-new: grep of .research/backlog.json for validuntil / fail-open / validateAccess returned no existing finding (the nfc rows on file cover revoke-offline-persistence, the 2KB SecureStore cap, and access-LOG parse — not the expiry comparison). Landable frontend-only remedy confined to NFCAccessController.ts: parse once to a timestamp and deny when non-finite, e.g. `const exp = new Date(credential.validUntil).getTime(); if (!Number.isFinite(exp) || exp < now.getTime()) return credential_expired;`. Confidence medium: the fail-open is proven by static read of JS NaN-comparison semantics; whether a malformed validUntil actually reaches the device is data-dependent, so the trigger is latent rather than runtime-confirmed — but the blast radius (physical access granted on bad data) warrants the high score.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/qrcode/QRCodeScanner.ts:366-369 — getScanHistory() does `const stored = await AsyncStorage.getItem(SCAN_HISTORY_KEY); return stored ? JSON.parse(stored) : [];` with NO try/catch. A corrupted/partially-written SCAN_HISTORY_KEY blob makes JSON.parse throw, so getScanHistory() REJECTS.

Blast radius: getScanHistory is the single read path for scan history and is awaited by saveScanToHistory (:344-345, reads existing history before unshifting the new entry), getRecentScansCount (:382), and clearScanHistory's siblings. A corrupt blob therefore not only breaks the history view but also prevents RECORDING any new scan (saveScanToHistory throws before it can rewrite the key), and the only recovery is an uncaught rejection surfacing to the caller — the store never self-heals.

This is the same CLASS as the already-landed done row code-review-mobile-rn-nfc-accesslog-parse-unguarded but in a DIFFERENT file (qrcode/QRCodeScanner.ts vs nfc/), and the self-healing remedy is already modeled in-repo by features/layout/layoutCache.ts:22-26 (catch -> removeItem -> return null). Net-new for this file: grep of .research/backlog.json for scanhistory / QRCodeScanner / getScanHistory returned nothing. Landable frontend-only remedy confined to QRCodeScanner.ts: wrap the parse in try/catch, `await AsyncStorage.removeItem(SCAN_HISTORY_KEY)` on failure, and return []. Verifiable by seeding AsyncStorage with a non-JSON SCAN_HISTORY_KEY and asserting getScanHistory()/saveScanToHistory() resolve rather than reject. Confidence medium (crash path proven statically; needs a corrupt blob to trigger).
